Question B-006-011-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Stacking two identical antennas ideally adds about 3 dB. 10 dBi + 3 dB = 13 dBi before real-world losses.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "13 dBi": Correct. Add about 3 dB to 10 dBi for two identical stacked antennas: 13 dBi.
- sourceIndex 1: "7 dBi": This subtracts 3 dB instead of adding the stacking gain.
- sourceIndex 2: "20 dBi": This doubles the dBi number arithmetically; decibels are logarithmic, so doubling power is about +3 dB.
- sourceIndex 3: "10 dBi": This ignores the ideal stacking gain.
